name: Shock conditions

subjectOf.text: The aftermath of a financial crisis creates shock conditions that constitute a suboptimal environment for rulemaking.
subjectOf.abstract: The aftermath of financial crises creates suboptimal conditions (shock conditions) for rulemaking.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857
scope_conditions: period immediately following a financial crisis

subjectOf.text: Post-crisis rulemaking occurs in an economic, political, and legal environment whose sense of urgency prevents a full evaluation of the consequences of new rules for all affected constituencies.
subjectOf.abstract: Rulemaking takes place in an economic, political, and legal environment that creates a sense of urgency for rulemaking and may not permit a full evaluation of the possible consequences for all constituencies.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857

subjectOf.text: The shock conditions that trigger calls for rulemaking have typically not been analyzed or absorbed systematically, so rulemaking under those conditions is associated with high levels of incomplete information.
subjectOf.abstract: Shock conditions that call for rulemaking often have not been appropriately analyzed and absorbed in a systematic fashion and are, thus, often associated with high levels of incomplete information.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857
scope_conditions: rulemaking triggered by an unabsorbed shock
